annotationRationale: Count ordered transformation sequences using rotation addition and coordinate reflections. The two routes classify whole triples or force the final move from the first two.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Geometry is appropriate because compositions of rigid motions determine which sequences qualify. No subject repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: Independent count gives 12, choice A. The unequal distances of the nonzero vertices force a returning transformation to fix both vertices individually. The statement, examples, choices and key agree; no figure is needed.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: Both useful accessible routes are retained: classify complete triples and force the third move from an ordered pair. The supplied group-theory presentation adds no necessary accessible route.
review.annotationCheck: Combined counting is appropriately assessed, with rotation properties and coordinate reflections as support. Both methods use all three immediate nodes; no contextual tags are needed.
review.areaCheck: Geometry is appropriate because compositions of rigid motions determine which sequences qualify. No subject repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Fixing the origin and the two vertices forces the identity. Orientation requires zero or two reflections. With zero reflections, quarter-turn sums must be 4 or 8, giving only the multisets (1,1,2) and (2,3,3), each with three orders. With two reflections, an odd quarter-turn exchanges axes and cannot work; a half-turn requires one reflection across each axis. Their six orders all work, totaling 12.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The stated basis accurately identifies nonofficial AoPS Solutions 1 and 2. The explanation uses original prose and supplies explicit axis and sign arguments for ordering issues.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The fixed-vertex reduction, orientation split, rotation sums and sign-change argument are explained sufficiently for an AMC 10 learner. No advanced prerequisite or additional diagram is required.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_h232 covers the disjoint cases and ordered counts; cnm_245 supports rotation effects; cnm_136 directly covers the axis-reflection sign rules.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The three exact native links fit the counting, rotation and coordinate-reflection steps. This problem exercises selected applications rather than every mastery criterion.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: 8.G.A.3 and 6.NS.C.6b fit the coordinate sign rules. G-CO.B.6 and the 8.G.A.1 links offer limited rigid-motion overlap; experimental verification and general angle or parallel-line properties are not assessed. cnm_h232 has no supplied US link.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: All immediate nodes are supported and appropriately specific. Combined counting is central, with the two geometry nodes serving as support.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The identity requirement makes the third transformation uniquely determined. Since the allowed set is closed under inversion, a pair qualifies exactly when its composition is allowed. Of nine rotation pairs, three are identity pairs, leaving six. Mixed pairs contribute four half-turn/axis-reflection pairs; odd quarter-turns produce unavailable diagonal reflections. Two distinct axis reflections contribute two more pairs. Thus 6+4+2=12.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The claimed LIVE reference supplies precisely the forced-inverse route. Its third-party status and source-informed-original basis are accurate; the candidate independently develops the composition checks.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The inverse criterion and all three pair types are justified. Coordinate rules explain why diagonal reflections are excluded, so the count is reconstructible without group theory.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_h232 matches classification and ordered-pair counting. cnm_245 and cnm_136 match the rotation compositions and reflection-coordinate calculations.
